messages:
maria: noticing a big provisioning failure in us-west2, GPU allocs failing with node-level IO errors. high latency + write errors coming from /var/scratch/tmp

sre-bot: anomaly detected: ephemeral-nvme iops +420% across scratchpool-us-west2 (alert id: ai-4872)

josh: which nodes are hit? can you paste a small lsof or kernel log?

maria: nodes: gnode-uw2-12, gnode-uw2-17, gnode-uw2-23, gnode-uw2-45. sample from gnode-uw2-12:
```
/var/log/syslog: kernel: blk_update_request: I/O error, dev nvme0n1, sector 123456789
/usr/local/bin/batch_preprocess.py[2234]: open files 120184, writing tmp files to /var/scratch/tmp/
```

eva: pattern looks like a tempfile leak from batch-preprocess. workers spawn lots of small temp files and do not unlink on crash. that will thrash the FS and cause metadata pressure.

raj: our ephemeral-cleaner has been running full scrubs every 5m. concurrent jobs=64. that combined with workers creates a write/read storm.

maria: current config snippet: `ephemeral-cleaner.retention=24h`, `ephemeral-cleaner.concurrent=64`, cron=*/5 * * * *

josh: propose immediate config change: retention -> 1h for scratchpool during burst window, concurrent -> 8, and add file-glob 'tmp*' priority purge. also add backoff when kernel reports I/O errors.

eva: +1. also patch batch_preprocess to use `tempfile.NamedTemporaryFile(delete=True)` or write to TMPDIR and atomic-move. quick fix: catch exceptions and ensure unlink in finally.

oncall: temporary mitigation plan: cordon gnode-uw2-12 and restart batch pod, patch cleaner config via configmap, roll a canary on one node then expand. minimal impact expected to running jobs.

maria: rollout plan: update configmap -> restart ephemeral-cleaner daemonset on one node -> wait 10m monitor iops and GPU alloc success. do 1 node/hr to avoid mass reprovisioning. expected disruption ~30s per node for daemon restart.

sre-bot: estimated cost hit during incident window (2h) due to GPU idle + overprovision: ~$3,200. see dashboard: https://redwood.internal/dashboards/iops-spike

josh: I'll open a PR for config + hygiene patch and link runbook steps. tagging @oncall for rollout coordination.

maria: assigned. please also add an alert for temp-file growth rate and lsof-based leak detection. thanks all :thumbsup:
